purpose: Which metric and which issue lights up where in the body, finer than the five contract regions. Research spec for the body map; read by UI code as static reference data. No value from crew_data.json is copied here.
rules: Status colour comes only from crew_data.json status and core/scoring. This file only says where to draw it.
A metric fills its own contract region (structures, parts). Parts listed under context belong to another region: draw them as a neutral outline or leader target, never in a status colour.
Panel copy comes from crew_data.json metrics[key].explain. The why lines here are for tooltips and the Systems screen; quote as a claim only when claim_ok is true.
Patterns with triggerable false or "context" must not raise an alert: the file has no metric for them.

model.note: Seen from the front (camera on +z), +x is on the right of the screen. The body stands on y = 0, centred on x = z = 0.

known_defects.issue: Six of the 20 structures are not bones. The build filter matches "tibia" inside "iliotibial tract", "tibialis anterior" and "tibialis posterior". Leave them out of any bone highlight (use metrics.bone_loss_pct.parts), or fix the filter and rebuild.
Muscles tagged "skeletal" in the atlas ended up in the bones node.
Laryngeal, nasal and costal cartilages are in the bones node. Harmless for a skeleton look.
Not brain tissue (a ganglion behind each eye, a dura fold, the top of the spinal canal). Cosmetic.

highlight.finding: The GLB has 7 nodes and 7 meshes, one merged mesh per node. No per-structure nodes or names exist inside it. The triangle order of the source atlas survived the merge and simplification, so a structure is one contiguous triangle range: 515 of 528 structures verified. Names come from the BodyParts3D part index (atlas.json) that the build script reads.
highlight.method: structure_index[node] gives each structure as t = [first_triangle, triangle_count]. In three.js: geometry.addGroup(t[0] * 3, t[1] * 3, materialIndex) on the node mesh, or write a per-vertex attribute for those triangles and tint in the shader (one draw call per node).
highlight.fallback: Where t is null (range not verified) use the bounding box b = [min, max] as a shader mask.
highlight.verification: A range is kept only if every triangle in it lies within 3 mm of the atlas bounds of that part, the range reaches those bounds within 4 mm, and it overlaps no other range.
highlight.validity: Ranges are valid only for the GLB with the sha256 above. If the GLB is rebuilt, regenerate this file.

field_notes.structures: Exact GLB node (mesh) names to highlight.
field_notes.parts: Atlas structure names inside each node; "all" means the whole node. Look each name up in structure_index for its triangle range.
field_notes.focus: Subset of parts to brighten when this metric is the selected one.
field_notes.context: Parts in another contract region; outline only.
field_notes.anchor: Callout leader end point, model space, metres. A real vertex of the mesh unless stated.
field_notes.label_side: Side of the screen for the callout in the front view.
field_notes.view_deg: Suggested orbit angle: 0 front, 90 body-left side, 180 back.
field_notes.measure_site: Where the reading is taken, from how_to_measure in crew_data.json. null when the file names no body site.
field_notes.localisation: target_organ, whole_body, or illustrative (a team choice, not a sourced anatomical claim).
field_notes.claim_ok: true when the why line uses wording from THESIS-DETAILS section 11.

hr.why: In flight the heart pumps more per beat (stroke volume +35%) at an unchanged resting rate; the rate rises on standing after landing.

bp_sys.why: 24-hour blood pressure runs 8-10 mmHg lower in flight and plasma volume falls about 15% within 2 days.

bp_dia.why: Pressure in the arteries between beats; systemic vascular resistance falls 39% in flight.

glucose.why: Insulin resistance rose in flight in all 8 crew of a 6-month ISS study.

temp.why: Resting core temperature runs about 1.0 C higher after 2.5 months in orbit.

sleep_h.localisation_note: The body clock sits in the hypothalamus (general anatomy, team choice). The pineal body is in the atlas but not in the GLB.
sleep_h.why: ISS crews average 6.1 h/night vs 8.5 h scheduled.

mood.localisation_note: Frontal and limbic areas stand for mood (general anatomy, team choice). Mood is a self-report, not a brain measurement.
mood.why: Isolation and confinement: stress, low mood and anxiety are common in flight.

exercise_min.why: Exercise is the main countermeasure against bone and muscle loss: about 2 h a day on the station.

bone_loss_pct.localisation_note: Anchor is the proximal right femur (hip). The femoral neck is not a separate part; the femur is one structure.
bone_loss_pct.why: About 1% per month at weight-bearing sites without exercise.
bone_loss_pct.caution: Do not derive a monthly rate from the app series (THESIS-DETAILS section 12, bone coefficient).

measure_site.label: Personal dosimeter
measure_site.note: Wear position is not stated in any source; chest is a placeholder.

dose_mSv_day.why: Dose rate jumps when solar particles arrive; crew dose from the reference storm (Oct 1989) must stay below 250 mSv.

measure_site.label: Personal dosimeter
measure_site.note: Wear position is not stated in any source; chest is a placeholder.

dose_mSv_cum.why: Mission total against the NASA-STD-3001 career effective dose limit (value: career_limit_mSv in crew_data.json).

issue_patterns.label: Fluid shift
issue_patterns.note: No fluid or face-swelling metric in the file. Show as context on a heart or blood-pressure flag, never as its own alert.
issue_patterns.why: Fluid moves toward the head in microgravity; plasma volume falls about 15% within 2 days.

issue_patterns.label: Eye (SANS)
issue_patterns.note: No vision metric in the file and no eye mesh in the GLB. The anchors are the eyeball centres (vitreous body) from the atlas. Nearby parts that do exist: optic chiasm, optic tracts, occipital lobes, orbit bones.
issue_patterns.why: About 70% of long-duration crew show at least one sign of SANS.

issue_patterns.label: Sleep debt
issue_patterns.note: Primary driver sleep_h. The simulated crew links sleep to mood (+0.4) and to heart rate (-0.3), so a sleep flag may travel with those.
issue_patterns.why: ISS crews average 6.1 h/night vs 8.5 h scheduled.

issue_patterns.label: Isolation strain
issue_patterns.why: Isolation and confinement: stress, low mood and anxiety are common in flight.

issue_patterns.label: Heart deconditioning
issue_patterns.note: Aorta is context only (it belongs to the blood region).
issue_patterns.why: The heart and vessels adapt to weightlessness: stroke volume +35%, vascular resistance -39%.

issue_patterns.label: Standing tolerance
issue_patterns.note: Needs a stand test (lying vs standing), which is not in the file. Relevant on the Moon and Mars surface environments.
issue_patterns.why: Blood volume is about 15% lower, so blood pools in the legs on return to gravity.

issue_patterns.label: Bone loss
issue_patterns.note: Highlight the 14 true bones only (see model.known_defects).
issue_patterns.why: About 1% per month at weight-bearing sites without exercise.

issue_patterns.label: Muscle loss
issue_patterns.note: Exercise minutes are a proxy; the file has no strength or muscle-mass metric.
issue_patterns.why: Without gravity, bones and muscles weaken quickly; exercise is the main countermeasure.

issue_patterns.label: Radiation storm
issue_patterns.note: Also driven by the warning level from storm_forecast.json. Whole-body aura; no single organ.
issue_patterns.why: Crew dose from the reference storm (Oct 1989) must stay below 250 mSv.

issue_patterns.label: Career dose
issue_patterns.note: Fill the silhouette as a gauge: dose_mSv_cum over career_limit_mSv, both read from the file.
issue_patterns.why: NASA-STD-3001 sets a career effective dose limit.

issue_patterns.label: Glucose drift
issue_patterns.note: Anchor is the vessel point nearest the pancreas centre from the atlas.
issue_patterns.why: Insulin resistance rose in flight in all 8 crew of a 6-month ISS study.

issue_patterns.label: Fever signal
issue_patterns.note: Whole-body aura, warm side of the status colour only.
issue_patterns.why: Resting core temperature runs about 1.0 C higher in orbit, so a jump above the personal band matters more than the absolute value.

issue_patterns.label: Kidney stone risk
issue_patterns.note: No hydration metric in the file and no kidney mesh in the GLB. The renal arteries and veins in the blood node mark the site.
issue_patterns.why: Urine volume falls by up to 47% early in flight; stones are a leading modelled cause of medical evacuation.

issue_patterns.label: Back pain

bones: Intervertebral disk of first lumbar vertebra
Intervertebral disk of second lumbar vertebra
Intervertebral disk of third lumbar vertebra
Intervertebral disk of fourth lumbar vertebra
Intervertebral disk of fifth lumbar vertebra

issue_patterns.note: No symptom metric in the file. Geometry is complete (lumbar vertebrae, disks, back extensors).
issue_patterns.why: Back pain is reported by 52% of crew in flight days 2-5.

issue_patterns.label: Motion sickness
issue_patterns.note: No symptom metric in the file. The inner ear is not in the atlas; the temporal bones that house it are in the bones node.
issue_patterns.why: Space adaptation sickness affects 70-90% of crew in the first days.

issue_patterns.label: CO2 headache
issue_patterns.note: Needs a cabin CO2 channel and a symptom report; neither is in the file.
issue_patterns.why: Headaches appear at cabin CO2 of 2.8-4.5 mmHg; 19 of 49 astronauts reported them.

gaps.fix: Add an "eyes" node in build_aegis_body.py (system "sensory"). Check the right sclera and right cornea first: their bounds in the atlas index reach across the midline (x = +0.031), which points to stray geometry.

gaps.fix: Add to the blood region as its own node.

gaps.atlas_parts: Pineal body, Pituitary gland (system "endocrine", so the brain filter skipped them)
optic nerve (the brain filter drops every name containing "nerve")
gaps.fix: Whitelist "optic nerve" in the brain filter.

gaps.needed_for: SpO2, cabin CO2 (not in the file today)
gaps.atlas_parts: Trachea and bronchial tree only; no lung surface
gaps.fix: Bronchial tree is enough for a clinical look; a lung surface would need modelling.

gaps.organ: Bone marrow, lymph nodes, thyroid gland
gaps.fix: Keep radiation as a whole-body aura.
Use the proximal-femur anchor; a box mask on the top 7 cm of the femur isolates it.

blender.reason: Every structure this spec needs either exists in the GLB as a triangle range or exists in the atlas and can be added by extending build_aegis_body.py (Python, trimesh). That is a rebuild, not modelling.
recommended_rebuild: Export one named node per structure (or keep 7 nodes and write the triangle ranges to a manifest) so names survive without this index.
Fix the load-bearing filter so "tibia" does not match tibialis or iliotibial.
Add nodes: eyes, kidneys (with ureters and bladder), pancreas; add pineal body, pituitary gland and optic nerves to brain.
where_blender_would_help: Look only: a smoother, watertight skin shell and a softer silhouette for the glass effect.
Baked ambient occlusion or vertex colours so organs read at projector distance.
A lung surface, which the atlas does not have.
Draco or meshopt compression of the 7.2 MB file.
